mission: 'We are working toward better conceptual understanding, algorithmic techniques, and policies to make AI more safe and socially beneficial.' Led by Dylan Hadfield-Menell in MIT CSAIL's Embodied Intelligence Group, it studies how humans and AI interact in value learning, incentives, recommendation, debugging and policy. Founding year approximate (Hadfield-Menell joined MIT ~2021).

key_work.title: Open Problems and Fundamental Limitations of Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
key_work.plain_summary: A widely cited survey (led by Stephen Casper) of why RLHF — the main way chatbots are aligned — has deep limits and cannot be the only safety layer.

key_work.title: The Off-Switch Game
key_work.plain_summary: A game-theory model showing an AI that is uncertain about human goals has an incentive to let humans switch it off.

key_work.title: Inverse Reward Design
key_work.plain_summary: Treats a designer's reward function as evidence of what they want rather than the literal truth, so agents behave cautiously in unfamiliar situations.

key_work.title: Consequences of Misaligned AI
key_work.plain_summary: Shows mathematically that optimising an incomplete proxy objective can make the true outcome arbitrarily bad — a formal version of Goodhart's law.

key_work.title: Defending Against Unforeseen Failure Modes with Latent Adversarial Training
key_work.plain_summary: Attacks a model's internal representations during training to make it robust to failures nobody thought to test for.

people.role: Group lead; associate professor, MIT CSAIL
Former PhD student (now Harvard Kennedy School)

warnings.text: Optimising an incomplete proxy for what humans want can make outcomes arbitrarily bad (Consequences of Misaligned AI).
RLHF has fundamental limitations and cannot alone ensure AI systems are safe (Open Problems in RLHF).
Post-training alone can't fix alignment problems (Hadfield-Menell talk, 2026).

recommendations.text: Design AI to remain uncertain about human objectives so it defers to oversight, including being switched off.
Use defence in depth and transparency/auditing requirements rather than relying on RLHF alone.
